## Feedback and overlays

Alerts, toasts, progress, loading, skeletons, tooltips, popovers, dialogs, drawers, empty and error states.

### Alert (`alert`)

An inline status message with a mandatory glyph on the status tint behind a 1px status border; role alert for danger, status otherwise. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, hover, focus-visible.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| danger.bg | `color.status.danger.tint` | `#2b0e0d` | use |
| danger.border | `color.status.danger.border` | `#e53935` | use |
| danger.text | `color.status.danger.text` | `#f73f35` | use |
| warning.bg | `color.status.warning.tint` | `#1f1a0c` | use |
| warning.border | `color.status.warning.border` | `#c9973f` | use |
| warning.text | `color.status.warning.text` | `#c9973f` | use |
| success.bg | `color.status.success.tint` | `#0f1a0e` | use |
| success.border | `color.status.success.border` | `#86a46f` | use |
| success.text | `color.status.success.text` | `#86a46f` | use |
| info.bg | `color.status.info.tint` | `#0f141c` | use |
| info.border | `color.status.info.border` | `#7e9ebb` | use |
| info.text | `color.status.info.text` | `#7e9ebb` | use |
| neutral.bg | `color.status.neutral.tint` | `#241010` | use |
| neutral.border | `color.status.neutral.border` | `#a3676b` | use |
| neutral.text | `color.status.neutral.text` | `#bd787d` | use |
| body.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| close.text | `color.action.tertiary.text` | `#e99499` | use |
| close.bg-hover | `color.action.tertiary.hover-bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| close.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |

#### Purpose

A status message that belongs to the page or form around it: a failed
submit, a saved draft, a deprecation notice. It stays in flow, is never timed,
and is announced once when it appears. Transient confirmations are toasts;
blocking questions are dialogs.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy. Each of the five statuses uses its own
`tint`, `border` and `text` roles.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | status tint, 1px status border, glyph and title in the status text colour | the glyph ✕ ! ✓ i · |
| hover | close button → {color.action.tertiary.hover-bg}; the alert itself does not react | cursor: pointer on the button only |
| focus-visible | 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} ring at −2px on the close button | the ring |

No disabled, selected or loading state: a message that is no longer true is
removed, not greyed.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. Escape does nothing so a page-level Escape handler is
never swallowed.

#### Accessibility

Danger is `role="alert"` (assertive) because it needs attention now; the
other four are `role="status"` (polite). The container exists before its text
is set so the live region fires; never inject text together with the
container. The glyph is `aria-hidden` and the title states the status in
words ("Build failed", "Saved"), so nothing depends on colour or the glyph
alone. The close button is at least 24×24 CSS pixels. Text meets 4.5:1 on
every tint; borders 3:1.

#### Portability

The glyph is a text character, not an icon font. A toolkit with a native info
bar maps its type to the five statuses and keeps the glyph in the text; one
without a tint draws the border only and records the deviation.

#### Non-examples

A coloured left stripe with no border. A rounded, shadowed card. A banner
that slides in or auto-dismisses. Colour-only status without the glyph and a
worded title. `role="alert"` for success. A close icon with no accessible
name. Fixed-position alerts covering content.

| count.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| stack.z | `z.toast` | `40` | use |

#### Purpose

A short notice that belongs to no one element on the page: "Saved",
"Copied", "Connection lost". It leaves on its own after a pause or when
dismissed. A decision is a dialog; a notice tied to a form is an alert.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy. The danger toast is the historical critical
notification: {color.status.danger.fill} with {color.status.danger.on-fill}
for the text, the glyph and both buttons.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | canvas surface, 1px overlay border, glyph in the status text colour | the glyph; the worded text |
| hover | action → {color.interaction.hover.bg} with {color.text.link-hover}; Dismiss → {color.action.tertiary.hover-bg}; the timeout pauses | cursor: pointer; the action's underline thickens |
| focus-visible | 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px on the focused button, {color.status.danger.on-fill} on the danger fill; the timeout pauses | the ring |
| stacked | one column, 4px gap, newest at the end; the last visible toast shows "+n" in {color.text.muted} | the count text; at most three visible |
| reduced-motion | no transition; present or absent | `prefers-reduced-motion`; nothing moves |

No disabled, selected or busy state.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. F6 is the web reference's shortcut; the timeout pauses
while a toast has focus or the pointer.

#### Accessibility

The text states the outcome in words; the glyph is `aria-hidden`. Every toast
has Dismiss; the timeout, at least 8 seconds, is extended for toasts with an
action, and an action is never the only way to reach what it does. Text
meets 4.5:1 on the canvas, on its tint and on the danger fill; borders, and
the danger fill against the canvas, 3:1.

#### Portability

Hosts with a notification daemon send the text and urgency instead of
drawing a toast. Toolkits with a native toast overlay use it and record that
the danger fill is not available.

#### Non-examples

A toast that slides in. A rounded, shadowed pill. No Dismiss and gone in two
seconds. Taking focus on appearance. More than three stacked with no count. A
form error as a toast. Colour-only status without the glyph and worded text.

### Progress (`progress`)

A native progress element with a label and value; determinate fills with the primary colour, indeterminate shows static 45° stripes, never an animation. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, busy, error, reduced-motion.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| track.bg | `color.interaction.pressed.bg` | `#420f0c` | use |
| track.border | `color.border.control` | `#a3676b` | use-and-report (D-007) |
| value.bg | `color.action.primary.bg` | `#7d1310` | use |
| value.bg-error | `color.status.danger.fill` | `#dc282e` | use |
| stripe.a | `color.action.primary.bg` | `#7d1310` | use |
| stripe.b | `color.interaction.pressed.bg` | `#420f0c` | use |
| label.text | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| value.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| detail.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| error.text | `color.status.danger.text` | `#f73f35` | use |

#### Purpose

Shows how far a known task has gone, or that an unbounded one is running. It
reports; it never blocks. A cancellable task has a button beside the bar. A
short wait with no bar is the loading indicator.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | {color.action.primary.bg} fill on the track; the value text | the native value; the percentage text |
| busy | static 45° stripes of {color.action.primary.bg} on {color.interaction.pressed.bg} across the track; no value text | `aria-busy`; `aria-valuetext`; the stripe pattern; no animation |
| error | fill → {color.status.danger.fill}; the label gains ✕ in {color.status.danger.text}; the detail line says what failed | glyph; worded detail |
| reduced-motion | identical to default and busy: nothing animates in any state | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

Indeterminate work is the busy state; the determinate variant enters it while
the total is unknown and leaves it once known.

#### Keyboard

None; a cancel button beside the bar has its own tab stop.

#### Accessibility

The value is in the native `value` and repeated in text. Indeterminate bars
set `aria-valuetext` ("Preparing"); the container sets `aria-busy` for the
duration. Completion and failure are announced through a polite live region,
not by the bar. Text meets 4.5:1; the track boundary and error fill 3:1. The
primary fill against the track is waived because the value is stated in
text.

#### Portability

A toolkit with a native bar maps the fill to the primary colour and disables
pulse animation; one without gradients draws the stripes with a hatched brush
or alternating characters.

#### Non-examples

A spinner. Animated or barber-pole stripes. A shimmering skeleton instead of
a bar. A circular ring. A rounded pill bar. Colour-only failure without the
glyph and text. A bar with no label. A bar that blocks input.

### Loading indicator (`loading-indicator`)

A static ⋯ glyph with a worded label inside an aria-busy container; inline next to text or as a centred block. There is no spinner. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, reduced-motion.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| glyph.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| label.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| block.bg | `color.surface.default` | `#100c0c` | use |
| block.border | `color.border.divider` | `#2b0e0d` | use-and-report (D-008) |

#### Purpose

Marks the wait between a request and its result when there is nothing to
measure: a list being fetched, a field being validated. There is no spinner;
the static ⋯ a loading control shows appears here beside a worded label.

#### Anatomy

Inline, glyph and label follow the text they qualify; as a block they sit
centred, inside a {color.border.divider} edge, where the content will appear.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | the static ⋯ and the label | `aria-busy="true"`; the glyph; the worded label |
| reduced-motion | identical: nothing to reduce | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

Not a control: no hover, focus or disabled state.

#### Keyboard

Never focusable. When loading replaces content that had focus, focus moves to
the container's heading or parent region, never the indicator, and returns to
the result when it arrives.

#### Accessibility

`aria-busy` lets assistive technology wait for the subtree to settle and
announce the label once. The label names the object ("Loading fonts") and is
always visible, inline as in a block; the glyph never appears without it. Nothing
moves, so there is no reduced-motion branch to get wrong. Label and glyph meet
4.5:1.

#### Portability

Text only; a toolkit's spinner widget is not used. A host that insists on an
activity indicator records the deviation and keeps it within the 150 ms
motion budget with a reduced-motion branch.

#### Non-examples

A spinner or rotating ring. Animated dots. A shimmering skeleton. A
full-page overlay blocking input for a fetch. A glyph with no label. An
indicator that takes focus. A dimmed, reduced-opacity container.

### Tooltip (`tooltip`)

A short description of a control shown on hover and focus; role tooltip linked by aria-describedby, a 1px overlay border on the raised surface, no arrow. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, hover, focus-visible, open, closed.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| popup.bg | `color.surface.raised` | `#160b0b` | use |
| popup.border | `color.border.overlay` | `#e53935` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| popup.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| shortcut.text | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| shortcut.border | `color.border.control` | `#a3676b` | use-and-report (D-007) |
| trigger.text | `color.action.tertiary.text` | `#e99499` | use |
| trigger.bg-hover | `color.action.tertiary.hover-bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| trigger.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |
| popup.z | `z.popover` | `10` | use |

#### Purpose

Describes a control without being its name: what an icon button does, its
shortcut, why it is disabled. Anything needed to use the control belongs in
the control or its label; anything interactive is a popover.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy; no arrow, shadow or radius.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | trigger at rest; popup shown for the demonstration | `aria-describedby` on the trigger |
| hover | trigger background → {color.action.tertiary.hover-bg}; popup after 300 ms; it hides 300 ms after the pointer leaves trigger and popup | cursor: pointer; the popup |
| focus-visible | 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px on the trigger; popup at once | the ring; the popup |
| open | popup visible, 1px {color.border.overlay} on {color.surface.raised} | popup in the accessibility tree |
| closed | popup absent; trigger unchanged | `hidden`; the description is still read from the DOM |

The popup has no hover, pressed or focus state; it is not interactive.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. Escape does nothing else, so a dialog behind the
trigger stays open. The popup never receives focus and contains nothing
focusable.

#### Accessibility

The popup stays open while the pointer is over the trigger or the popup
(WCAG 1.4.13: hoverable, dismissible, persistent). The trigger has its own
accessible name; the tooltip never supplies it. Touch has no hover: offer the
description by long-press or inline. Text meets 4.5:1; the popup border and
the shortcut border 3:1.

#### Portability

A bordered box of text; placement is the host's positioning primitive. A
toolkit with a native tooltip uses it with the border and background tokens
and records any radius it cannot remove.

#### Non-examples

A rounded bubble with an arrow. A shadow, or a fade longer than 150 ms. The
tooltip as an icon button's only accessible name. A link or button inside.
Opening on focus but not hover, or on hover with no delay. A `title`
attribute. Following the pointer.

### Dialog (`dialog`)

A native dialog on the overlay surface behind a 1px overlay border and the backdrop; modal when shown, with trapped focus and Escape to close. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, open, closed, focus-trapped, hover, focus-visible, reduced-motion.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| root.bg | `color.surface.overlay` | `#241010` | use |
| root.border | `color.border.overlay` | `#e53935` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| root.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring-container` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| root.z | `z.dialog` | `30` | use |
| title.text | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |

| close.text | `color.action.tertiary.text` | `#e99499` | use |
| close.bg-hover | `color.action.tertiary.hover-bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| close.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |
| button.text | `color.action.secondary.text` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| button.border | `color.action.secondary.border` | `#a3676b` | use |
| button.bg-hover | `color.action.secondary.hover-bg` | `#630f0d` | use |
| primary.bg | `color.action.primary.bg` | `#7d1310` | use |
| primary.text | `color.action.primary.text` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| primary.bg-hover | `color.action.primary.hover-bg` | `#911410` | use |
| destructive.bg | `color.action.destructive.filled-bg` | `#dc282e` | use |
| destructive.text | `color.action.destructive.filled-text` | `#f9faf9` | use |
| destructive.bg-hover | `color.action.destructive.hover-bg` | `#dc282e` | use |
| field.bg | `color.surface.input` | `#000000` | use |
| field.border | `color.border.control` | `#a3676b` | use-and-report (D-007) |
| field.label | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| note.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |

#### Purpose

A question or small task the page cannot continue without: confirm a
destructive action, name a new profile, sign in again. It takes the whole
screen's attention, so it is short, clearly titled and always offers a way
out.

#### Anatomy

Confirmations take no fixed tone (D-015): an ordinary one uses primary, a
destructive one the filled destructive button. The form variant holds a
labelled text field on {color.surface.input}.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | the dialog open on its backdrop | `open`; the page behind is inert |
| open | as default; opacity 0 → 1 within 150 ms on capable hosts | `open`; focus inside the dialog |
| closed | dialog and backdrop absent | no `open`; focus back on the opener |
| focus-trapped | when it holds focus, the dialog carries the container ring, 2px solid {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} at −3px; the note says Tab cycles | Tab never leaves; the note text |
| hover | Close → {color.action.tertiary.hover-bg}; other buttons take their tone's hover | cursor: pointer |
| focus-visible | 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px on the focused control; primary uses {color.interaction.focus.ring-container}, destructive {color.action.destructive.filled-text} (D-015) | the ring |
| reduced-motion | no opacity transition; present or absent | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

A dialog is never disabled; a busy dialog disables its confirm button and
shows the ⋯ glyph on it.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. Enter on the dialog itself never triggers a destructive
confirm. On open, focus goes to the first focusable element, or to the
dialog when that element is destructive.

#### Accessibility

Title and first paragraph link through `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby`. The theme never re-implements the trap
on a non-modal dialog. The backdrop is decorative and cancels on click only
when Close is also present. Text meets 4.5:1; the overlay border and rings
3:1.

#### Portability

A toolkit with a native modal window uses it with the overlay border on the
frame and records that the backdrop is the host's; one without a top layer
draws the backdrop as a full-window overlay under the dialog.

#### Non-examples

A glowing or shadowed card. Rounded corners. Sliding or scaling in.
`<dialog>` shown with `show()` and a hand-written trap. No title, or the
title only in the accessible name. A destructive confirm as the default
Enter action. A backdrop that closes the dialog with no Close button. A
dialog stacked on a dialog.

### Drawer (`drawer`)

A full-height modal panel anchored to the start or end edge; a native dialog on the overlay surface with a 1px overlay border on its inner edge. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, open, closed, focus-trapped, reduced-motion.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| backdrop.bg | `color.surface.backdrop` | `rgb(0 0 0 / 65%)` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| root.bg | `color.surface.overlay` | `#241010` | use |
| root.border | `color.border.overlay` | `#e53935` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| root.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring-container` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| root.z | `z.drawer` | `20` | use |
| title.text | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| text.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| body.divider | `color.border.divider` | `#2b0e0d` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| item.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| item.bg-hover | `color.interaction.hover.bg-strong` | `#630f0d` | use |
| item.text-hover | `color.text.link-hover` | `#f4eeee` | use |
| close.text | `color.action.tertiary.text` | `#e99499` | use |
| close.bg-hover | `color.action.tertiary.hover-bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| close.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |
| note.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |

#### Purpose

A modal dialog shaped as a full-height side panel, for navigation or a task.
Below 900px the sidebar collapses into a drawer; above it, a drawer holds
tasks that need more room than a dialog.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy; the overlay border is the only visible edge.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | the panel open at its edge on the backdrop | `open`; the page behind is inert |
| open | as default; opacity 0 → 1 within 150 ms on capable hosts; never a slide | `open`; focus inside the panel |
| closed | panel and backdrop absent | no `open`; focus back on the opener |
| focus-trapped | while it holds focus, the panel carries the 2px solid {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} ring at −3px; the note says Tab cycles | Tab never leaves; the note text |
| reduced-motion | no opacity transition; present or absent | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

Items take the states of their list or navigation; Close takes the tertiary
button's hover and ring.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. On open, focus goes to the first focusable element, the
first item or Close.

#### Accessibility

Named by its title through `aria-labelledby`. Never re-implement the trap on
a non-modal element or a plain aside. The backdrop is decorative; a click on
it may close the drawer only because Close is also present. Logical
properties mirror the panel and its border in RTL. Text meets 4.5:1; the
border and ring 3:1.

#### Portability

Toolkits without a top layer draw the backdrop as a full-window overlay under
the panel; toolkits with a native sidebar keep it non-modal and record that it
is a sidebar, not a drawer.

#### Non-examples

A panel that slides in. A shadow or a rounded inner corner. A plain aside
with a hand-written focus trap. A bottom sheet with a drag handle. No Close
button. A drawer that stays open under a dialog. A translucent panel over page
content.

### Empty state (`empty-state`)

What a container shows when it has nothing to list; a glyph, a heading in the bright text colour, one sentence in the muted colour and an optional secondary action. Family: feedback. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| root.bg | `color.surface.default` | `#100c0c` | use |
| root.border | `color.border.divider` | `#2b0e0d` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| glyph.text | `color.icon.decorative` | `#a3676b` | use |
| heading.text | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| text.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| action.text | `color.action.secondary.text` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| action.border | `color.action.secondary.border` | `#a3676b` | use |
| action.bg-hover | `color.action.secondary.hover-bg` | `#630f0d` | use |
| action.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |

#### Purpose

Replaces a blank pane, an empty table body or a filtered-out list: it says
what is empty and offers the one action that changes it, when there is one. A
failure is the error state; a wait is the loading indicator.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | glyph, heading and sentence centred; the action, when present, below them | the worded heading; the action is a real button |

No states of its own; the action takes the secondary button's hover and ring.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. When a filter empties a list that had focus inside it,
focus moves to the region's heading, not into the empty state, so the person
hears where they are.

#### Accessibility

The heading is a real heading at the region's level, so the empty state
appears in the outline; the sentence follows it in reading order. When
content becomes empty after an action (filter, delete), a polite live region
announces the heading text. The action is never the only route: filters can
also be cleared where they were set. Text meets 4.5:1; the action border 3:1.

#### Portability

A toolkit with only a placeholder string adds the action as a separate button
below the view.

#### Non-examples

An illustration or mascot. A primary (filled) call to action. A blank pane. A
greyed-out table header with no message. Only "No data". A heading in the
accent red. An empty state shown while loading. Centred text in a rounded,
shadowed card.

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### Portability

#### Non-examples

Unlabelled controls. Colour-only status. Drag-only operations. Hidden

### Error state (`error-state`)

A specific failure explanation with an explicit recovery request. Family: feedback. Priority: R2. Maturity: stable. States: default, error, loading, disabled, focus-visible.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |

#### Purpose

Explains a failed operation and asks for an explicit recovery; it never
claims the service recovered.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Danger border and text heading. Its buttons are the secondary button (button.md). | Specific written explanation and error glyph. |
| error | Same explicit failure treatment. | Failure text remains available. |
| loading | Busy status accompanies the existing explanation. | aria-busy and host-provided pending text. |
| disabled | Disabled roles at full opacity. | Native retry button is disabled. |
| focus-visible | Dashed ring. | Native keyboard focus. |

#### Keyboard

As in the key table.

#### Accessibility

Never rely on colour or the glyph alone. Give the retry action a specific
name. Announce a new error in a host status region without repeatedly
interrupting reading. Keep focus unless recovery needs an explicit next step.

#### Portability

Follows the shared component defaults in `spec/portability.md` (section "Shared component defaults").

#### Non-examples

Unlabelled controls, colour-only status, drag-only operations, hidden required
instructions, stolen focus or an invented service success.

## Developer interfaces

Editor syntax, gutters, caret, selections, search, diagnostics, diffs, terminal text and the historical ANSI slots.

### Code editor (`code-editor`)

The editor surface, gutter, caret, current line, selection, bracket match and monochrome syntax roles that every code-editing or code-viewing host maps onto. Family: developer. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, focus-visible, selected, selected+container-inactive, current, read-only.

#### Purpose

The reference rendering of source code: the contract a real editor's theme
API is mapped onto. It never edits.

#### Anatomy

Root `.code-editor`; parts `.code-editor-<part>`: `-pre`, `-line`, `-ln`
(line number), `-text`, `-indent`, `-ws` (rendered whitespace), `-caret`,
`-sel` (selection range), `-bracket`, `-fold`, `-fold-gutter`. Syntax spans
are `.code-editor-<role>`: `-kw` keyword, `-str` string, `-cm` comment,
`-num` number, `-const` constant, `-fn` function, `-var` variable, `-type`,
`-op` operator, `-punct` punctuation, `-prop` property, `-heading`, `-tag`,
`-attr` attribute, `-esc` escape, `-invalid`, `-deprecated`.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | code on {color.code.bg}; comments italic; invalid text wavy-underlined in {color.code.syntax.invalid}; deprecated text struck through | italic, wavy underline, line-through |
| focus-visible | 2px {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} ring at −3px; 1px {color.code.caret} bar; caret line filled {color.code.current-line} across gutter and text, its number {color.code.line-number-active} | the ring; the caret bar |
| selected | range filled {color.code.selection-bg}; syntax colours kept | the host's selection is announced; the fill spans line ends |
| selected+container-inactive | same range in {color.interaction.selection.inactive-bg} with {color.interaction.selection.inactive-text}; no caret, no ring | lightness drop between the two fills |
| current | both characters of the matched pair outlined 1px solid {color.code.bracket-match} | an outline box, not a colour change |
| read-only | gutter on {color.surface.sunken}, same line numbers; dotted gutter rule; no caret | `aria-readonly`; dotted rule; no caret |

Precedence: selection under the text, current line under the selection,
bracket outline and caret above everything. The caret never blinks in the
reference; a host that blinks it follows the user's cursor-blink setting and
stops under reduced motion.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. The theme only draws what the host's keys produce; the
read-only reference consumes no key. A host that captures Tab offers Escape,
then Tab, and announces it.

#### Accessibility

Syntax colour is decoration; meaning never rides on colour alone (italic
comments, wavy-underlined invalid text, struck-through deprecated text).
Selection is a fill and focus a ring, drawn together, never substituting for
each other. Every syntax role meets 4.5:1 on {color.code.bg}. Inside
{color.code.selection-bg}, D-029 keeps keyword, tag, property and heading at
4.5:1; comment and type text fall below it, a recorded limitation of the
selection value, never fixed by recolouring tokens locally. The reference
stays monochrome; a host that wants hue maps {color.code.hued.string} and the
other opt-in `code.hued.*` roles (D-030), which meet 4.5:1 inside the
selection. Line numbers are text people read and meet the text floor; indent
guides, rendered whitespace and the gutter rule are decorative. In forced
colours the caret, selection and bracket outline take `Highlight`; syntax
spans keep their text styles.

#### Portability

The port maps these roles onto the host's theme API without touching caret
behaviour, keyboard handling or selection semantics. No bracket-match
outline: bold weight, deviation recorded. No 1px caret: the host's own caret
in {color.code.caret}. The `heritage-ansi` and `extended` profiles change
role values only, never the mapping.

#### Non-examples

Rainbow syntax in the reference, or any hue beyond the three bounded ones
(hosts opt into `code.hued.*`, D-030). A blinking or animated caret in the
reference. A selection that turns text white and drops the syntax roles. A
current line brighter than the selection. A bracket match as a background
fill, which reads as a selection. Line numbers in a decorative colour. A glow,
gradient or rounded corner on the box. Removing the host's focus indicator
without drawing the container ring.

### Diagnostics (`diagnostics`)

Inline problem markers in code (underline patterns, an error line and an overview stripe) and the problems panel that lists them as a listbox, each severity carrying its glyph. Family: developer. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, hover, focus-visible, selected, selected+focus-visible, error, empty.

| Part | Role | Value | Eligibility |

| root.border | `color.border.control` | `#a3676b` | use-and-report (D-007) |

| code.line-number | `color.code.line-number` | `#ad7175` | use |

| code.selection-bg | `color.code.selection-bg` | `#420f0c` | use |

| error.text | `color.diagnostic.error.text` | `#f73f35` | use |
| error.stripe | `color.diagnostic.error.stripe` | `#e53935` | use |
| error.line-bg | `color.diagnostic.error.bg` | `#2b0e0d` | use |

| row.location | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| row.divider | `color.border.divider` | `#2b0e0d` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| row.bg-hover | `color.interaction.hover.bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| row.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |
| row.bg-selected | `color.interaction.selection.bg` | `#531310` | use |
| row.text-selected | `color.interaction.selection.text` | `#f4eeee` | use |

#### Purpose

How problems appear on code and in the list that indexes them. Six kinds,
each told apart by pattern and glyph as well as colour. The panel is the
keyboard route to every marker.

#### Anatomy

Root `.diagnostics` with `.diagnostics-inline` or `.diagnostics-panel`.
Inline: `.diagnostics-code` (the `<pre>`), `-line`, `-ln`, `-text`, `-mark`
(the stripe cell) and the ranges `.diagnostics-error`, `-warning`, `-info`,
`-hint`, `-unused`, `-deprecated`; `.diagnostics-line-error` is the filled
row; `.diagnostics-target` is the range of the selected row. Panel:
`-header`, `-title`, `-count`, `-status`, `-list`, `-row`, `-glyph` (with
`-glyph-error` and so on), `-message`, `-loc`, `-rule`, `-empty`.
Patterns: error and warning wavy, info and hint dotted, unused dotted in
{color.diagnostic.unused.text}, deprecated line-through in
{color.code.syntax.deprecated}. Glyphs: `✕` error in
{color.diagnostic.error.text}, `!` warning in {color.diagnostic.warning.text},
`i` info in {color.diagnostic.info.text}, `·` hint in {color.text.subtle}.
The stripe mark repeats the glyph in the stripe colour
({color.diagnostic.error.stripe}, {color.diagnostic.warning.stripe}).

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | ranges decorated on {color.code.bg}; the error row filled {color.diagnostic.error.bg}; panel rows on {color.surface.default}, 1px {color.border.divider} between | underline pattern; glyph |
| hover | panel row → {color.interaction.hover.bg}; inline ranges unchanged (the hover tooltip is a host surface) | cursor: default on rows |
| focus-visible | active row: 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px; inline box: 2px {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} at −3px | the ring |
| selected | row filled {color.interaction.selection.bg}, text and glyph {color.interaction.selection.text}; the matching inline range filled {color.code.selection-bg} under its underline | `aria-selected`; the glyph stays; the fill spans the row |
| selected+focus-visible | the selection fill and 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px | both at once |
| error | provider failed: a `role=status` line with `✕` in {color.status.danger.text} above the stale rows; the stripe shows the same `✕` at its top | glyph; live announcement |
| empty | rows, stripe marks and inline decorations removed; `✓ No problems` in {color.text.muted}, glyph in {color.status.success.text} | glyph; the absence of decoration |

Precedence: selected > hover; focus-visible is drawn on top. A selected row
recolours its glyph to the on-selection text, so the shape, not the hue,
carries the severity.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table; next and previous problem and the hover card belong to
the host.

#### Accessibility

Never colour-only: the underline pattern in code, the glyph in the panel, and
the glyph is part of the option's accessible name ("Error: frmae is not
defined, title.js line 6"). The error row fill adds to the wavy underline,
never replaces it. Text, including unused code, meets 4.5:1; every underline
meets 3:1 on its actual background, the selected range included. The status
line is announced once. In forced-colours mode the patterns persist because
they are `text-decoration`, not backgrounds.

#### Portability

Where wavy is unavailable the port uses a plain underline plus the glyph and
records the deviation. Hosts with their own overview ruler map the stripe
colours; hosts without one omit the stripe and keep the glyphs.

#### Non-examples

Red-only errors without `✕` or the wavy pattern. Wavy for every severity.
Purple or cyan for info and hint. A row hover that changes only text colour.
A selected row whose glyph keeps its severity colour on the fill. A rounded
highlight or left accent bar instead of the row fill. Removing the error line
fill to "calm" the editor.

### Diff view (`diff-view`)

Unified and split diffs as native tables; added, removed and modified rows keep their textual gutter marker, word-level changes are underlines, conflicts are double borders. Family: developer. Priority: R1. Maturity: stable. States: default, hover, selected, focus-visible, expanded, collapsed.

| root.text | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| line-number.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| line-number.rule | `color.code.gutter-rule` | `#2b0e0d` | use |
| row.divider | `color.border.divider` | `#2b0e0d` | use-and-report (D-008) |
| added.bg | `color.diff.added.bg` | `#0f1a0e` | use |
| added.gutter | `color.diff.added.gutter` | `#86a46f` | use |
| added.emphasis | `color.diff.added.emphasis` | `#86a46f` | use |
| removed.bg | `color.diff.removed.bg` | `#2b0e0d` | use |
| removed.gutter | `color.diff.removed.gutter` | `#e53935` | use |
| removed.emphasis | `color.diff.removed.emphasis` | `#e53935` | use |
| modified.bg | `color.diff.modified.bg` | `#1f1a0c` | use |
| modified.gutter | `color.diff.modified.gutter` | `#c9973f` | use |
| hunk.bg | `color.diff.header-bg` | `#241010` | use |
| hunk.text | `color.text.muted` | `#bd787d` | use |
| hunk.context | `color.text.default` | `#e99499` | use |
| conflict.border | `color.diff.conflict-border` | `#f73f35` | use |
| conflict.marker | `color.text.bright` | `#ffa2a7` | use |
| fold.text | `color.text.link` | `#f73f35` | use |
| fold.bg-hover | `color.interaction.hover.bg-strong` | `#630f0d` | use |
| row.bg-hover | `color.interaction.hover.bg` | `#1c0a09` | use |
| row.ring | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |
| row.bg-selected | `color.interaction.selection.bg` | `#531310` | use |
| row.text-selected | `color.interaction.selection.text` | `#f4eeee` | use |
| row.ring-selected | `color.interaction.focus.ring` | `#e53935` | use |

#### Purpose

The `+`, `−` and `~` markers are content, present in every state and every
profile; word-level underlines leave the text contrast untouched.

#### Anatomy

Root `.diff-view` with `.diff-view-unified`, `-split`, `-word-level` or
`-conflict`. Rows: `.diff-view-row`, `-row-context`, `-row-added`,
`-row-removed`, `-row-modified`, `-row-hunk`, `-row-fold`, `-row-conflict`
(marker lines `-row-conflict-start`, `-mid`, `-end`). Cells: `.diff-view-ln`,
`-marker`, `-text`, `-fold-cell`, `-range` (the `@@` span). Split adds
`-side-old` and `-side-new`, and on a `-row-pair` `-cell-removed` and
`-cell-added` (an empty `-cell-blank` faces an added line); conflict adds
`-row-ours` and `-row-theirs`. Word spans: `.diff-view-word-added` (2px
underline in {color.diff.added.emphasis}) and `.diff-view-word-removed`
(underline plus line-through in {color.diff.removed.emphasis}). Fold:
`.diff-view-fold` with SVG chevron `.diff-view-chevron` and labels
`-fold-collapsed` and `-fold-expanded`; folded rows are `<tbody
class="diff-view-folded" hidden>`. Line numbers use {color.text.muted}, not
{color.code.line-number}, which falls below 4.5:1 on the modified fill.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | added {color.diff.added.bg}, `+` in {color.diff.added.gutter}; removed {color.diff.removed.bg}, `−` in {color.diff.removed.gutter}; modified {color.diff.modified.bg}, `~` in {color.diff.modified.gutter}; hunks {color.diff.header-bg}; conflicts in a 3px double {color.diff.conflict-border} | the markers; the double border |
| hover | number and marker cells → {color.interaction.hover.bg}; the text cell keeps its fill | cursor: default; hover-capable pointers only |
| selected | whole row {color.interaction.selection.bg} with {color.interaction.selection.text}; the marker stays | `aria-current` (or `:target` for a permalinked line); the marker glyph |
| focus-visible | 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px around the row, including a selected row | the ring |
| expanded | folded `<tbody>` shown; chevron down; "Hide 12 unchanged lines" | `aria-expanded="true"`; the rows appear |
| collapsed | folded `<tbody>` hidden; chevron to the inline end; "… 12 unchanged lines" | `aria-expanded="false"`; the ellipsis |

Precedence: selected > hover; focus-visible is always drawn. A selected row
loses its diff fill, never its marker.

#### Keyboard

A plain table has no row focus. The web distribution wraps it in a named,
focusable scroll region with the container focus ring, so wide lines can be
read without page overflow. The chevron turns within the motion budget.

#### Accessibility

Each marker sits in its own cell, so a screen reader announces `+` or `−`
before the line and monochrome print keeps the distinction. Word-level
changes use `text-decoration`, never a fill, so row text keeps 4.5:1 on
every diff fill. The `−` marker is a bold glyph on its own fill and is held
to the 3:1 graphics floor. Folded rows are `hidden`, not visually clipped,
so they are not read while collapsed. Conflict markers are the literal
`<<<<<<<`, `=======` and `>>>>>>>` lines.

#### Portability

Cell backgrounds, borders and text decoration exist in every toolkit. Without
double borders, draw two 1px lines and record it; without line-through, keep
the underline and the `−` marker. The three extension hues are confined to
the `diff` group and change with the profile; the markers do not.

#### Non-examples

Red and green fills without `+`/`−`. Word-level changes as a bright fill
that pushes text below 4.5:1. A removed line in `text.disabled` or struck
through whole. Collapsed hunks only visually clipped and still read out.
Purple conflict blocks. Hover that recolours the code text. Round-cornered
hunk cards. A selected row that drops the marker.

#### Purpose

The reference for terminal text. The sixteen slots, frozen in `Xresources`,
are the theme's origin: `heritage-ansi` carries them exactly; `default`
lifts the dim slots to readable values of the same hues (D-029) and makes
slot 6 coral (D-032). Programs choose their slots; the theme makes every slot
but the dim tier safe for text instead of steering them.

#### Anatomy

Root `.terminal` plus `.terminal-transcript`, `.terminal-ansi-grid` or
`.terminal-attributes`; parts `.terminal-line`, `-prompt` (`-prompt-path`,
`-prompt-branch`, `-prompt-arrow`), `-cursor`, `-sel`, `-label`, `-fail`,
`-bold`, `-dim`, `-italic`, `-underline`, `-inverse`, `-strike`. Each slot
class reads one role variable ({color.terminal.ansi.0} …
{color.terminal.ansi.15}), so a profile switch recolours without touching
markup. {color.terminal.prompt-bg} is the heritage dark red in every profile,
whatever slot 4 carries (D-032).

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | text on {color.terminal.bg}; cursor hollow, 1px {color.terminal.cursor} outline; no ring | the hollow cursor |
| focus-visible | 2px {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} container ring at −3px; cursor solid {color.terminal.cursor} with {color.terminal.bg} text | the ring; the cursor fills |
| selected | run filled {color.terminal.selection-bg} with {color.terminal.selection-text}; slot colours inside give way to the selection text | whole-cell fill; the emulator exposes the selection |
| busy | command running: solid static block cursor at the end of the output; transcript `aria-busy` | `aria-busy`; cursor shape; no blink |
| current | cursor line filled {color.code.current-line} across its width; cursor as in focus | row fill; cursor cell |

The reference cursor never blinks. A host keeps the user's blink setting and
stops it under reduced motion; the theme never turns it on.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. The reference transcript consumes no key; the theme
draws the ring, selection and block cursor where the host reports them.

#### Accessibility

In `default`, slots 1–7 and 9–15 meet 4.5:1 on the terminal background
(D-029); coral slot 6 sets highlighted names apart from rose text (D-032).
Slot 8 (dim tier) and slot 0 (the background) do not; the grid marks both
with `✕`. The crosses follow `default`, so under `heritage-ansi` (ten slots
fail) the sample text shows the failures. The `extended` overlay proposes a
semantic sixteen that all meet 4.5:1. The background row is not a contract:
the default foreground passes only on slot 0, the terminal background on
every slot but 0 and 8. Bold-as-bright and 256-colour or 24-bit sequences
bypass the slots and are outside the theme. Most emulators dim by mixing a
slot halfway into the background (dimmed slot 6 falls under 3:1); the theme
does not brighten slots to compensate, a host setting for dim text alone may
(D-032). Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are styles a screen reader
can expose.

#### Portability

Hosts that set the palette (Orca, Ghostty, Warp, CE Devbox's shell palette)
share one; the prompt is the one deliberate heritage-style exception, set in
24-bit {color.terminal.prompt-bg} and {color.terminal.prompt-text} whatever
the slots carry. CE Devbox's shell palette and its Agnoster directory and
virtualenv segments follow in that repository (D-029, D-032).

Any sixteen-slot emulator holds these values byte for byte; port evidence
records whether bold-as-bright is off and whether cursor and selection keys
exist. A port carries the slots unchanged; it may recommend `LS_COLORS` or a
prompt configuration but never changes slots to compensate. Cursor shape is the
user's; the theme supplies only its colour.

#### Non-examples

Normalising the heritage slots to 4.5:1 and calling it `heritage-ansi`. A
blinking cursor in the reference. A glowing bar cursor. Bold rendered as
bright. A purple or cyan slot borrowed from another scheme. Wrapping the
transcript and breaking the prompt segments. A selection drawn as a ring
instead of a fill. Rounded or gradient prompt segments.

#### Purpose

Finds literal text in a read-only code sample. Searching a list or a site is
the search-field.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Plain escaped source. Button controls are the secondary button (button.md); inputs keep the input look. | Readable preformatted text. |
| filled | Match fill; current match has its own marker. | Exact current and total counts. |
| no-results | No highlighted matches. | Explicit zero-results status. |
| focus-visible | Dashed control ring. | Native keyboard focus. |

#### Keyboard

As in the key table.

#### Accessibility

Render source as text, never as trusted HTML from the consumer. Highlighted matches must retain the exact source text for copying. Announce counts without moving input focus. Match navigation scrolls the current mark into view, and reduced motion requires no animation.

#### Portability

Follows the shared component defaults in `spec/portability.md` (section "Shared component defaults").

#### Non-examples

Unlabelled controls, color-only status, drag-only operations, hidden required instructions, stolen focus or an invented service success.

## Composed specimens

Settings panel, administrative form, filterable table, i3-inspired window frame; file browser, compact dashboard and form builder later.

#### Purpose

Proves the form components compose without new tokens, in every state and
at every width; it prescribes no product.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy; each uses its component's own markup and
classes.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | every component's rest tokens on {color.surface.default}; the open section carries the indicator bar | `aria-current` |
| focus-visible | the dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} on the focused control (shown on the first switch); others at rest | the ring |
| invalid | the inner-gap field takes the 2px {color.status.danger.border} and its ✕ message; others at rest | border width 1 → 2px; glyph; `aria-invalid` |
| busy | Apply shows the static ⋯ glyph in {color.action.primary.text}; the form carries `aria-busy`; nothing shrinks or animates | glyph; `aria-busy`; cursor: progress |

The composed components keep their own hover, checked, disabled and
read-only treatments; only the states the screen adds are declared here.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. Nothing traps focus and nothing changes on hover alone.

#### Accessibility

The nav has its own label, so two navigation landmarks on a page stay
distinguishable; the open section is `aria-current="page"`. `aria-busy` on the form announces the pending Apply without
a live region. Every control has a programmatic label; every message is
linked by `aria-describedby`. Text meets 4.5:1; control boundaries, the
indicator bar and the danger border 3:1.

#### Portability

The sidebar width is specimen layout too, not a rule. Toolkits port each
contained component through its own mapping and place them with their native
layout.

#### Non-examples

A rounded, shadowed settings card. A Material-style app bar above the form.
Pill switches or animated thumbs. Section links as filled tabs instead of
the indicator bar. A red form background for invalid. Dimming the controls
with opacity while applying. A spinner replacing the Apply label.

#### Purpose

A record screen proving that the advanced form components compose with the
navigation and feedback components, then the same screen at its review step.
It shows validation, saving and inertness across a whole form; it does not
prescribe a product.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy; each is the contained component's own markup
and classes.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | every component's rest tokens on {color.surface.default}; the current step carries the indicator bar, future steps are disabled | `aria-current="step"` |
| invalid | name and hostname take the 2px {color.status.danger.border} and ✕ messages; the current step's marker becomes ✕; a danger summary on {color.status.danger.tint} naming the two fields replaces the notice; other fields stay at rest | border 1 → 2px; glyphs; `aria-invalid`; `role="alert"` |
| busy | Continue shows the static ⋯ in {color.action.primary.text}; nothing shrinks or animates | glyph; `aria-busy` on the form; cursor: progress |
| disabled | every control takes its component's disabled treatment ({color.text.disabled}, {color.border.disabled}, {color.interaction.disabled.bg}); labels and review keys dim; no hover | `disabled` on the wrapping fieldset; cursor: not-allowed; never opacity |

Contained components keep their own hover, focus-visible, required,
placeholder-shown and read-only states; this table adds only the form-level
ones.

#### Keyboard

The region, the Breadcrumb navigation and the form are offered as landmarks
by name. In the review variant the Edit buttons are ordinary stops inside the
table. Nothing traps focus.

#### Accessibility

The h2 names both the region and the form. Complete steps read ", complete"
through a visually hidden suffix; future steps are disabled, not hidden. The
summary alert is announced once on submit; each field's message stays linked
by `aria-describedby`. Inside the disabled fieldset every control reports its
state natively. The review table has a caption, column headers and row
headers; each Edit button names its field through a visually hidden suffix.
Text meets 4.5:1 and the invalid boundary 3:1; disabled text is exempt (house
floor 3:1).

#### Portability

No script is needed to render any state. Toolkits port each contained
component through its own mapping.

#### Non-examples

A rounded card with a drop shadow. A Material stepper with numbered circles
and a connecting line. A red banner across the whole form instead of the
summary alert plus field messages. Field borders that glow red. A spinner
replacing the Continue label. Fields fading to half opacity while saving. A
sticky footer bar with a shadow.

#### Purpose

Proves that navigation, display and feedback components compose around one
data-table (find, filter, select, page), including nothing matching and still
loading. It shows a whole list screen's states; it does not prescribe a
product.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy; badges carry ✓ (Tested) and i
(Demonstrated). Every part is the composed component's own markup and
classes.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | each component at rest; Name sorted ascending with ▲; Prev disabled | `aria-sort`; the glyph |
| hover | the pointed row takes {color.interaction.hover.bg}; toolbar controls and chips hover only on their own pointer events | cursor |
| focus-visible | dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} on the focused row (the third in the specimen); toolbar and chips at rest | the ring |
| selected | two rows in {color.interaction.selection.bg} with {color.interaction.selection.text} and a checked box; select-all mixed with – | `aria-selected`; ✓ and – glyphs; `aria-checked="mixed"` |
| no-results | the body is the "No components match" row; count reads 0 of 43; the search status line announces it; chips stay so the cause is visible | text; `role="status"` |

The composed components keep their own pressed, sorted, disabled, loading
and open treatments; only the states the whole screen adds are declared here.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table, following the toolbar and data-table contracts. The
region, the search landmark and the pagination navigation are offered by
name. A disabled Prev is not focusable.

#### Accessibility

The search field's label and its status line are visually hidden so the
toolbar stays one row; the status line announces "No components match"
through `role="status"`. The count is a second status region and changes once
per filter. Rows are named by their Name cell through `aria-labelledby` on
the row checkbox. Badge glyphs keep status readable without colour. Text and
badges meet 4.5:1; boundaries and the ring on the selection fill meet 3:1.

#### Portability

Every state renders without script from the root hooks
`data-state-selected` and `data-state-no-results` and the table's own
`aria-busy`.

#### Non-examples

A rounded search pill with a magnifier in a shadowed toolbar. Chips as pills
with a coloured fill per category. Zebra-striped rows. A selected row shown by
a coloured left bar and no fill. A blue Material checkbox. A skeleton shimmer
while loading. Infinite scroll with no count and no pages.

#### Purpose

The frame the palette was tuned in. It proves that the terminal and
code-editor components sit in window chrome drawn from the same roles, and it
records the workstation's geometry as reference metrics. A specimen of
composition, not a desktop: only i3 and sway ports draw this frame.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | terminal window focused: {color.border.active} frame, bright title; editor at rest; workspace 1 filled | the title text; `aria-selected` |
| focus-visible | 2px {color.interaction.focus.ring-container} ring at −3px inside the focused window or container; the client draws no second ring | the ring |
| selected | workspace 2 takes the selection fill with {color.interaction.selection.text}, 1px dashed {color.interaction.focus.ring} at −2px when focused; workspace 1 at rest | `aria-selected` |
| container-inactive | no window focused: every frame {color.border.default}, every title {color.text.muted} on {color.surface.chrome}, tab indicator {color.border.selected-indicator-inactive}, no caret | lightness drop; no caret |
| error | workspace 3 urgent: {color.status.danger.fill} with {color.status.danger.on-fill} and a trailing ! | the ! mark; "urgent" read to assistive technology |

The clients keep their own states (the terminal's busy cursor, the editor's
selection and read-only gutter); only the states the frame adds are declared
here.

#### Keyboard

As in the key table. A window group can hold focus itself, as i3 focuses a
container. Nothing traps focus.

#### Accessibility

The region names its workspace and layout. The workspace tablist is named;
the status group is `lang="zh"`;
its Nerd Font glyphs are `aria-hidden`, so only the labels are read. Every
window is a named group; the focused and the floating window say so in their
names. Urgency carries the ! mark and a visually hidden "urgent". Text meets
4.5:1; frames, the ring and the urgent fill 3:1.

#### Portability

The geometry is recorded so a port of the i3 configuration matches the
workstation; any other application keeps its own window manager, bar and
gaps.

#### Non-examples

Rounded corners or a title-bar gradient. A focused window that glows or
blurs its neighbours. A shadow under a tiled window. 14/−2 gaps forced into
an unrelated application. A red underline instead of the selection fill for
the workspace. Traffic-light buttons in the title bar. A translucent bar.

#### Purpose

Finds a file by location and name; every file operation belongs to the
caller.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Locations and native file rows. Button controls are the secondary button (button.md); inputs keep the input look. | Explicit names, kinds and sizes. |
| selected | Selected location follows the tree contract. | aria-selected plus location filter. |
| empty | No file rows. | Explicit zero-files text. |
| no-results | Filtered rows are hidden. | Matching count and retained search query. |
| focus-visible | Dashed control outline. | Native focus and tree roving focus. |

#### Keyboard

As in the key table.

#### Accessibility

Keep the complete nested tree behaviour and semantic table headers.
Filtering does not move focus. Announce counts, and keep the search field
available after zero results. File actions never imply access beyond the
host's actual permissions.

#### Portability

Follows the shared component defaults in `spec/portability.md` (section
"Shared component defaults").

#### Non-examples

Unlabelled controls, color-only status, drag-only operations, hidden required instructions, stolen focus or an invented service success.

#### Purpose

A small operational overview of caller data; it fetches nothing and infers no
business health.

#### Anatomy

Parts as listed in the anatomy.

#### States

| State | Visual | Non-colour channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Square metric panels, readable tables. Its buttons are the secondary button (button.md). | Metric names, exact values, status text. |
| loading | Busy boundary; existing content kept. | `aria-busy` and host-provided loading status. |
| empty | Explicit absence of records. | Empty message; a zero metric differs from an unknown one. |
| focus-visible | Dashed action outline. | Native keyboard focus. |

#### Keyboard

As in the key table; nothing else is bound.

#### Accessibility

Metrics stay term/value pairs, tables are labelled and all chart data stays
visible. No colour-only health score. Busy status never implies a completed
refresh. The host words unknown metrics; never show them silently as zero.

#### Portability

Follows the shared component defaults in `spec/portability.md` (section
"Shared component defaults").

#### Non-examples

Unlabelled controls, color-only status, drag-only operations, hidden required instructions, stolen focus or an invented service success.

## Decisions

Statuses: `proposed` (awaiting the owner), `accepted`, `rejected`, `superseded`.
A token moves from `proposed` to `approved` only by an `accepted` decision referenced
in its `$extensions["io.github.j3w1.theme"].approval.decision`. Agents may open
`proposed` entries; only the owner changes a status.

Each entry has a Decision (what was chosen, with `Rule:` naming the section
that holds the rule), a Why (the reason and the rejected alternatives worth
remembering) and a Status line (status, date, who decided, and what later
entries changed). Computed ratios are in `exports/contrast.md`. Entries are
ordered by topic.
